summary: Among the supplied candidates, only four documents apply transformer-style self-attention encoder models directly to wildfire mapping, and one applies a graph-based method to the same task. [V0173] (Adebayo et al., 2026) is the strongest match: it explicitly presents self-attention encoder models for mapping active wildfire extent, evaluated on the FireScope dataset with AUROC 0.85. [V0174] (Brennan et al., 2018) also applies self-attention encoder models to mapping active wildfire extent, reporting F1=0.92 on ChurnBench. [V0175] (Chen et al., 2019) revisits active wildfire extent mapping with self-attention encoder models, evaluated on MetroFlow with accuracy 0.64. [V0176] (Duarte et al., 2020) applies self-attention encoder models to mapping active wildfire extent on the Atlas-ICU dataset, reporting MAE 0.71. As a fifth candidate, [V0171] (Brennan et al., 2018) applies message passing over relational graphs—a related but distinct neural architecture—to mapping active wildfire extent on MetroFlow, achieving F1=0.88. All other candidates either address unrelated tasks (hate speech, electricity, protein function, etc.) or use non-transformer methods on non-wildfire topics, and are therefore not directly relevant.
